findings.title: Group-wide canManage() grants manage rights to callers that only have VIEW permission
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (the no-arg, "all groups" variant), the permission check is `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` – i.e. it treats VIEW as sufficient to satisfy a manage check. Compare this with the per-group override `canManage(GroupModel group)` a few lines below, which correctly checks only `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE`. Because `requireManage()` (used e.g. by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() to guard creating top-level groups) ultimately calls this no-arg canManage(), any admin who was only granted the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource is incorrectly treated as having manage rights and can create/modify groups. This is a privilege-escalation bug; it should check AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE only, matching canManage(GroupModel).

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() passes the Resource's internal id instead of the group id, breaking the lookup and the returned ids
findings.body: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the lambda receives `groupResource` (a Resource found via findByType) and calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` and `granted.add(groupResource.getId())`. Everywhere else in this class (canView(GroupModel), canManage(GroupModel), canViewMembers, canManageMembers, canManageMembership) the lookup key passed to hasPermission is `group.getId()` – the actual GroupModel id, which is also the value AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() uses as the Resource's *name* when the resource is created. Resource.getId() is a separate, internally-generated identifier that does not equal the resource's name. As a result, the internal `hasPermission(groupId, ...)` call does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` with the wrong value, which will not find the correct resource and will instead always fall back to the catch-all "Groups" resource-type resource. In addition, the ids placed into the returned `granted` set are resource ids, not actual group ids, so callers (UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource) that use this set to filter by `UserModel.GROUPS` will never match real group memberships. This breaks per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS based user visibility for V2 admin permissions.

findings.title: getOrCreateResource() never tags per-resource instances with their resource type
findings.body: getOrCreateResource() creates per-instance resources (for Users, Clients, and now Groups) via `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, resourceServer.getClientId())` but never calls `resource.setType(resourceType)` on them, unlike the "all-resource" resources created in init() (which do call resource.setType(type)). Because of this, `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` used by the new GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() will not find individual per-group resources created through this method, since they were never tagged with the "Groups" type. This silently undermines any type-based resource queries introduced for the new Groups feature.

findings.title: Undocumented behavior change: canViewMembers(group) now also honors MANAGE_MEMBERS scope
findings.body: In GroupPermissions.canViewMembers(GroupModel), the scope check was widened from `hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE)` to `hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE, MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE)`. This is part of the stable (GA) ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature, not the new V2 feature this PR is adding. The PR description only mentions adding Groups resource type/scopes to the V2 authorization schema, so this silent semantic change to the existing V1 group-members view permission is undocumented and untested for V1 (the new tests target only the V2/KeycloakAdminPermissionsServerConfig path). Existing V1 deployments relying on manage-members not implying view-members will see a behavior change.

findings.title: Missing negative test that VIEW-only all-groups permission does not grant manage capability
findings.body: testManageAllGroups() only verifies that granting MANAGE on the all-groups resource allows creating/updating groups; there is no test asserting that an admin granted only VIEW on the all-groups resource is still forbidden from creating/updating/deleting groups. Such a test would have caught the bug in GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() where hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) incorrectly allows VIEW to satisfy a manage check.
